identity.title: ALMA Observations of the Water Fountain Pre-planetary Nebula IRAS 16342-3814: High-velocity Bipolar Jets and an Expanding Torus

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here, we report millimeter-wave molecular-line and continuum interferometric observations of IRAS 16342, using the Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA).

evidence.quote: IRAS 16342-3814 (hereafter IRAS 16342) is the best studied and nearest ($\sim$2 kpc) water-fountain PPN.
IRAS 16342-3814 (hereafter IRAS 16342) is the best studied and nearest ($\sim$2 kpc) water-fountain PPN.

question.value: What are the structure, kinematics and mass-loss history of the water-fountain pre-planetary nebula IRAS 16342-3814 (jets, torus, AGB envelope, central continuum source), and what do they imply for the jet-launching binary models?

evidence.quote: We have mapped $^{12}$CO J=3–2 and other molecular lines from the “water-fountain" bipolar pre-planetary nebula (PPN) IRAS 16342-3814 with $\sim0.35\ensuremath{''}$ resolution using ALMA.
This paper uses ALMA dataset ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00678.S.
The data were obtained on 2015, June 13 with 37 antennas of the ALMA 12 m array in band 7.

findings_qualitative.value: Binary models with BHL wind accretion and wind RLOF are ruled out; enhanced RLOF or common-envelope accretion needed

evidence.quote: Enhanced RLOF from the primary (i.e., at the Red Rectangle level: BL14), or accretion within CE evolution appear to be the most likely candidates

claims.hypothesis: Is a torus and high-velocity jet formed soon after a sharp AGB mass-loss increase?
claims.experiment: Derived expansion ages of AGB CSE, EHVO, torus and HVO from ALMA CO and H13CN data
claims.result: AGB CSE ~455 yr, EHVO 130-305 yr, torus 160 yr, HVO ~110 yr
claims.finding: Torus and HVO formed a few hundred years after a sharp increase in mass-loss rate

evidence.quote: This sequence suggests that the torus and HVO were formed a few hundred years after a sharp increase in the mass-loss rate of the progenitor AGB star.

claims.hypothesis: Does the mm continuum imply large grains?
claims.experiment: Compared 0.89 mm flux with model and single-dish fluxes; derived beta and dust mass
claims.finding: Substantial mass of mm-sized grains, if thermal dust

evidence.quote: Testing alternatives to the large-grain model, such as spinning dust and magnetic nanoparticles (e.g., Draine & Hensley 2012), will require continuum measurements at additional mm-submm wavelengths.

claims.hypothesis: What accretion mode can power the HVO?
claims.experiment: Scaled the HVO accretion rate relative to CRL 618 using BL14
claims.finding: BHL and M-WRLOF ruled out for WD and MS accretors

evidence.quote: Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton (BHL) wind accretion and wind Roche lobe overflow (M-WRLOF) accretion are ruled out, for both white-dwarf and main-sequence accretors.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Radiation pressure cannot drive the HVO (timescale too long, >7.3e3 yr)

evidence.quote: The HVO cannot be driven by radiation pressure because its dynamical (expansion) time-scale is much smaller

evidence.quote: the assumption of a uniform radial outflow velocity is likely not strictly true, and the derived ages are somewhat uncertain
